conventions.convention: A Yang–Baxter operator is invertible. Non-strict formulas are transported through strong monoidal constraints.
Tensor powers are left-nested; the zeroth tensor power is the unit.

A positive strand points in increasing height. Crossing superscripts specify geometry independently of orientation; mixed signs reverse the oriented crossing sign. Framings and isotopies are relative to fixed boundary collars.
Absolute simplicity means End(X)=k·id_X with id_X≠0; it does not assert simplicity in an arbitrary abelian category.
The pivotal comparison is j=uθ. The trace evaluates a map into the double dual; the empty closed braid has value 1.
Positive stabilization inserts the curl evaluated by θ_X, giving λ; negative stabilization gives λ⁻¹. Scalar extraction requires bilinear tensor product.
The tangle presentation and evaluator assume countable choice. Unframed closure invariance assumes AC through Markov's theorem. No nonzero categorical dimension is required for invariance.
Rational representations are natural actions on all commutative k-algebras, not just k-points; coactions are right coactions V→V⊗A. Faithfulness means injectivity on every algebra-valued point group.
Unipotence is the fixed-vector property for every nonzero rational representation. It imposes no smoothness, connectedness or reducedness.
Derived subgroups and normality are scheme-theoretic and are tested on all base algebras.
Borels are smooth connected solvable subgroup varieties, geometrically maximal among that class; arbitrary infinitesimal overgroups are excluded from maximality.
Hochschild cochains are natural transformations on algebra-valued points. Long exact sequences require degreewise surjective cochain maps; linear coefficients satisfy this condition.

Section conjugacy requires smooth D or smooth connected U. Full maximal-diagonalizable classification requires smooth connected U; smooth D alone permits only the smooth-diagonalizable classification.

load_bearing.statement: For every finite subset S of a comodule M over a commutative Hopf algebra over a field, there is a finite-dimensional subcomodule N containing S. Consequently M is the directed union of its finite-dimensional subcomodules. No basis of A and no choice principle is used.

For an affine finite-type group scheme G over a field, the stated construction is a bijection, natural in V and G, between coordinate-Hopf-algebra comodule structures on V and rational representations on V, and maps subcomodules to subrepresentations. With ρ(e_j)=Σ_i e_i⊗a_ij, Δ(a_ij)=Σ_l a_il⊗a_lj, ε(a_ij)=δ_ij, and the associated comorphism sends x_ij to a_ij. No choice principle is used.

Assuming AC, DG is closed, normal and characteristic, and G/DG is commutative. Smoothness and connectedness of G respectively imply those properties for DG. Every closed subgroup containing DG is normal. Abstract commutators on every base algebra lie in DG; for smooth G over algebraically closed k, DG(k)=[G(k),G(k)]. For smooth connected solvable G≠1, DG≠G and dim DG<dim G.

For an affine finite-type group scheme over any field, coconnected coordinate Hopf algebra implies unipotence without choice. Under AC, unipotence, a closed embedding into some U_n, coconnected coordinate Hopf algebra, and existence of a faithful finite-dimensional unipotent representation are equivalent. No smoothness, connectedness or perfectness is assumed.

Without choice, trigonalizability is equivalent to triangularity of every finite-dimensional representation; a normal unipotent subgroup with diagonalizable quotient implies trigonalizability, and quotients are trigonalizable. Under AC these are also equivalent to a closed embedding into some T_n; closed subgroups and field extensions preserve trigonalizability.

Assume AC for the geometric suppliers. A smooth connected solvable affine algebraic group over a field acting on a nonempty complete finite-type scheme has a point over an algebraic closure fixed by all algebraic-closure points of the group. Over an algebraically closed field the fixed point is rational.

Assume AC. For a trigonalizable group over a perfect field, the extension by its largest normal unipotent subgroup splits if the field is algebraically closed, if that subgroup is smooth connected, or if the diagonalizable quotient is connected. A smooth connected trigonalizable group over an algebraically closed field is G_u⋊T for each maximal torus T, and its maximal tori are G_u(k)-conjugate.

Assume AC and algebraically closed k. For trigonalizable G with unipotent kernel U and diagonalizable quotient D, sections exist without smoothness. They are U(k)-conjugate if D is smooth or U is smooth connected. If U is smooth connected, maximal diagonalizable subgroups are exactly section images. If only D is smooth, this conclusion concerns maximal smooth diagonalizable subgroups. For smooth G, maximal tori are s(D°) for full sections and are U°(k)-conjugate.

Assume AC. For a finitely generated commutative Hopf algebra A over a field, Spec A has a closed immersion into GL_V for some nonzero finite-dimensional V, which may be chosen inside the regular representation. The same conclusion holds for every affine finite-type group scheme.

Assume AC. Closed subgroup schemes of an affine finite-type group scheme correspond bijectively to Hopf ideals of its coordinate algebra; the inverse is Spec(A/I), and the correspondence reverses inclusions.
For every n≥2, a Yang–Baxter operator R on an object X gives a unique homomorphism B_n→Aut(X^{⊗n}) sending σ_i to R_i. These satisfy ρ_{n+1}(ι_nβ)=ρ_n(β)⊗id_X.

Under countable choice, every framed oriented tangle is an elementary word. Turaev's reduced relations (3.2.a)–(3.2.h), together with the defining expressions for redundant orientation variants, give a complete presentation: two words represent the same tangle exactly when those relations and the strict monoidal axioms relate them.

Under countable choice, for n≥1 the ribbon trace t_n(β) equals the framed-tangle evaluator on the blackboard-framed closure. Positive and negative stabilization add the respective signed curl; the positive curl evaluates to θ_X.

Under countable choice, in a k-linear ribbon category with bilinear tensor product and End(1)=k, an absolutely simple X with θ_X=λid_X satisfies t_{n+1}(ι_nβσ_n^{±1})=λ^{±1}t_n(β), for n≥1, with the declared curl convention.

concerns.concern: The Statement allows V=0. Proof 1.1 takes a basis and invokes T_n, but def-upper-unitriangular-group-scheme defines T_n only for n≥1. The zero representation is trivially triangular; an explicit zero-dimensional case closes this small proof boundary.

seams_checked.note: Opened the action, stabilizer, orbit, dimension and coset-quotient suppliers. Actual uses preserve smoothness; dimension/minimal-orbit uses occur with connected G over algebraically closed k on reduced classical orbit closures. Nonsmooth stabilizers remain allowed.

Checked all three citing items. GL coordinates and its automorphism functor are used in finite dimension; bracket uniqueness uses the faithful closed immersion with AC retained. Hopf multiplication is evaluated on all base algebras.

Checked the citing definitions, Facts and relevant proof clauses. Finite-subcomodule, Hopf-ideal and matrix-coefficient clauses preserve their domains. Nonaffine representation uses explicitly supply their morphism convention instead of applying an affine comodule dictionary.
GL and rational-representation uses preserve finite dimension and the matrix-point convention. Finite regular submodule uses retain the exact finite-subset conclusion.

Checked citing clauses for unipotence, weights, derived groups, stable central G_a, Borel fixed points, complete quotients and torus conjugacy. Geometric Borel applications retain algebraic closedness and smooth connected affine groups; arbitrary-field conclusions name additional descent or split-group suppliers.

Both citing items use finite-dimensional rational representations on every base algebra. The projective-line supplier correctly distinguishes P(V∨) from the quotient convention P(V); homogeneous-space construction imposes smoothness on G without imposing it on H.
